newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia court postpones EU ratification decision.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia court postpones EU ratification decision.

text.p: The Constitutional Court has postponed ruling whether a constitution that still bars foreigners from buying land conflicts with Slovenia's plans to become an associated state of the European Union.
Slovenia has promised the EU it will change its constitution to allow foreigners to own property within four years of the association pact taking effect.
But opposition parties have argued that ratification of the EU accord would contravene the constitution unless the real estate rule were amended first.

The government asked the Constitutional Court to decide and Janez Cebulj, secretary of the court, told Reuters on Thursday: "The court decided to postpone the decision until the next session, which will take place at the latest on June 5, in order to get the opinions of experts in international law."
Parliament must wait for the court's go-ahead before taking a vote to ratify the association agreement, which was signed in June last year.
European Commission President Jacques Santer said in April that speedy ratification was a condition for Slovenia to be included in the first round of nations to start negotiations on EU membership.
